subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Tiwanaku: City Above the Clouds
description: A quick, practical guide to Tiwanaku: City Above the Clouds.

hook.text: At 12,600 feet above sea level in Bolivia, an ancient city defied logic by thriving where crops barely grow.

buildup.text: Tiwanaku flourished from 500 to 1000 CE near Lake Titicaca, with monumental stone architecture and raised fields.

discovery.text: The Gate of the Sun is carved from a single block of andesite, featuring a central figure scholars still debate.

twist.text: The Inca claimed Tiwanaku was where the world began. They borrowed heavily from its art and mythology.

climax.text: A prolonged drought around 1000 CE dried up the farmland. The city was abandoned within a generation.

punchline.text: A civilization that thrived in thin air was brought down by thin rain.

quiz.question: What likely caused Tiwanaku's collapse around 1000 CE?
options: The Inca conquered and forcibly relocated the population
A prolonged drought dried up the farmland
A volcanic eruption made the region uninhabitable

details.summary: Tiwanaku, at 3,850 meters above sea level near Lake Titicaca in Bolivia, was the capital of a powerful pre-Inca civilization that thrived from about 500 to 1000 CE. Its monolithic stone gateways, sunken temples, and precision masonry demonstrate sophisticated engineering at extreme altitude.
details.whyItMatters: Tiwanaku proves that a major civilization could thrive at extreme altitude. Its influence spread across the Andes and likely inspired Inca architectural and political traditions centuries later.
takeaways: Located at 3,850 meters of altitude near Lake Titicaca in Bolivia
A powerful pre-Inca capital flourishing from about 500 to 1000 CE
Features precision masonry and monolithic stone gateways

faq.question: How did people farm at Tiwanaku's extreme altitude?
faq.answer: They developed raised field agriculture — elevated planting surfaces separated by water channels. The water absorbed solar heat during the day and released it at night, protecting crops from altitude frost. This system sustained a city of perhaps 20,000 people at nearly 4,000 meters elevation.

faq.question: What is the Gateway of the Sun?
faq.answer: A monolithic stone archway carved from a single block of andesite, featuring a central figure — possibly the creator deity Viracocha — surrounded by winged attendants. The gateway was found broken and out of its original position, but remains Tiwanaku's most iconic monument.
